// diagnostic

E-WEB-CROSS-PARTITION

`wasm_caller` is compiled to Wasm but calls `js_helper`, which lives in JS

What

`wasm_caller` is compiled to Wasm but calls `js_helper`, which lives in JS

Why

The web backend keeps DOM/view code in JS and compute in WASM; a direct call across that boundary is not allowed yet. A `jet build --target=web` run reports this web-target diagnostic.

Fix

Move the call behind a generated bridge, colocate both functions in the same bucket, or adjust their `#Target(Wasm|JS)` markers

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E-WEB-CROSS-PARTITION: tests/ui/app_capability_target.stderr.

Error [jet.AppFeatureNotOnTarget]: App feature `.csr` needs target `JS`, but the resolved target is `Wasm`.
  --> tests/ui/app_capability_target.jet:4:22
    |
  4 | fn run() { web.app().csr().serve() }
    |                      ^^^
 Why: App is one type across targets, but each feature must be supported by the target selected by `#Target` or the package manifest; rejecting it in sema keeps AOT, JIT, interpreter, and web codegen on one meaning (I9). During `jet check`, Jet reports this diagnostic.
 Fix: Choose a build target that supports `.csr` (for example `#Target(JS)` for browser features or a native target for server features), or remove that feature.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E-APP-TARGET-FEATURE

Error [jet.WebPartitionCrossed]: `run` is compiled to Wasm but calls `App::serve`, which lives in JS
  --> tests/ui/app_capability_target.jet:4:4
    |
  4 | fn run() { web.app().csr().serve() }
    |    ^^^
 Why: The web backend keeps DOM/view code in JS and compute in WASM; a direct call across that boundary is not allowed yet
 Fix: Move the call behind a generated bridge, colocate both functions in the same bucket, or adjust their `#Target(Wasm|JS)` markers
